architecture_chain: release_archive.py: deterministic ZIP_STORED canonical whole-archive construction + exact verifier
release_artifact_subject.py: locally derived exact unopened artifact subject after archive verification
artifact_bound_clean_machine.py: every clean-machine row binds the same exact artifact subject
receipt_content_binding.py: external receipt exact bytes must equal the locally expected canonical ArtifactBoundPreHandoffReceipt bytes
PORTABLE_HOST_HARNESS_AND_DISTRIBUTION_CONTRACT.md: user hands one release package to a capable local coding agent; receiving agent verifies release/pre-handoff identity before installation

threat_analysis.threat: accidental or adversarial mutation of the handed-off ZIP or receipt bytes after the expected subject is established
malicious wholesale replacement of both artifact and self-consistent receipt by an untrusted distributor
threat_analysis.current_f2: content self-consistency alone does not prove producer identity; an external trust anchor would be required if this threat enters scope

threat_analysis.threat: rollback/freeze/mix-and-match in a long-lived public update repository
threat_analysis.current_f2: not covered by a one-off signature alone; TUF-class version/expiry/snapshot/root semantics are the relevant mechanism if an updater/repository is later introduced

external_mechanism_mapping.slsa: Separates envelope signature/root verification from subject-digest matching. Useful model if F2 later consumes non-recomputable producer provenance from an untrusted channel.
external_mechanism_mapping.sigstore_cosign: Can sign/verify blobs and attestations with identity-bound certificates and transparency evidence, but introduces identity provider/root/transparency/bundle lifecycle and should not be a mandatory dependency for the current offline/local one-handoff gate absent an explicit origin-authentication requirement.
external_mechanism_mapping.dsse: Provides a compact authenticated payload+payloadType envelope if F2 later needs signed semantic attestations; it does not define the trust root by itself.
external_mechanism_mapping.tuf: Appropriate for an actual update/repository threat model with rollback/freeze/mix-and-match concerns; disproportionate for the current single handoff before such a distribution channel exists.

smallest_future_mechanism_if_origin_auth.name: DistributionTrustAnchor/v1
levels: L0 current: direct trusted user handoff plus deterministic local recomputation; document this trust assumption explicitly
L1 bounded: out-of-band trusted pin of artifact_sha256 and prehandoff_receipt_sha256; zero new signing stack
L2 public/untrusted distribution: authenticated DSSE/Sigstore-style signed subject with explicit expected signer identity/root and offline-verifiable bundle
L3 update channel: TUF-class root/targets/snapshot/timestamp semantics for freshness, rollback and repository consistency

decision.reason: The next declared WP1110 discriminator is executable: create/identify the final deterministic ZIP and external canonical receipt, then collect real clean-machine observations. A signing stack does not increase information gain for that immediate gate unless the owner/product threat model first declares an untrusted distribution/origin-authentication requirement.

recommended_documentation_delta: Make the current distribution trust assumption explicit: the one-handoff package is owner/trusted-channel supplied. If this assumption changes, promote DistributionTrustAnchor/v1 research before public distribution rather than silently treating self-consistent receipts as publisher authentication.
next_exact_gate: Do not delay first real clean-machine acceptance for signature infrastructure. Preserve origin-authentication as a named deferred security hypothesis and re-open only when public/untrusted distribution, auto-update, mirror, or independent producer-identity verification becomes a product requirement.
